content.text:
No, it isn't. `src/services/user-service.js` still uses callbacks and imports `query` and `update` straight from `../db.js`. The comment at `src/services/user-service.js:3` says so too: "Chapter 5 migrates this to UserRepository."

`src/repositories/user-repository.js` already has a promise-based `UserRepository` with a method for each service function:

| user-service.js (callback) | UserRepository (promise) |
|---|---|
| `listActiveUsers(callback)` | `findActive()` |
| `findUser(id, callback)` | `findById(id)` |
| `softDeleteUser(id, when, callback)` | `softDelete(id, when)` |

The queries are identical on both sides, so switching over shouldn't change behaviour. What will change is the function signatures: callers in `src/api/routes.js` and `tests/user-service.test.js` would need to move from callbacks to promises.

The project has a `migrate-module` skill for exactly this. It moves one service onto its repository and then runs that module's tests. I can run it on `user-service.js` if you want.
